Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 83, verse 1–6:

Tafsir of Surat al-Mutaffifin

It is Madani.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Aqil informed us (Ibn Majah added: and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr), they both said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Yazid—that is Ibn Abi Sa'id al-Nahwi, client of Quraysh—from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, they were among the worst of people in measuring. So Allah revealed: ﴿Woe to those who give less [than due]﴾, and after that they became good in measuring [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11654) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2223).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn al-Nadr ibn Hammad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Hilal ibn Talq, who said: While I was traveling with Ibn 'Umar, I said: Who are the people with the finest appearance and the most complete measure? The people of Makkah or Madinah? He said: They deserve it. Did you not hear Allah say: ﴿Woe to those who give less [than due]﴾?

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Dirar, from 'Abd Allah al-Muktib, from a man, from 'Abd Allah, who said: A man said to him: O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, indeed the people of Madinah give full measure. He said: And what prevents them from giving full measure when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: ﴿Woe to those who give less [than due]﴾, until He reached: ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/58).]].

Thus, what is meant by tatfif (giving less, deficiency) here is defrauding in the measure and the scale, either by taking more when taking from people, or by giving less when giving to them. For this reason, Allah, Exalted is He, explained the mutaffifin, whom He promised loss, destruction, and woe, by His saying: ﴿Who, when they take a measure from people, take in full﴾, meaning: they take their right completely and in excess, ﴿but when they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss﴾, meaning: they give less. It is best that "kalu" and "wazanu" be read as transitive, with "hum" in the place of the object (accusative), while some take it as an emphatic pronoun for the implicit subject in "kalu" and "wazanu", with the object omitted because the context indicates it; both are close in meaning.

Allah has commanded fulfilling the measure and the scale, saying: ﴿And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is better and more favorable in outcome﴾ [al-Isra': 35], and He said: ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice; We do not burden any soul except to its capacity﴾ [al-An'am: 152], and He said: ﴿And establish the weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient﴾ [al-Rahman: 9]. Allah destroyed the people of Shu'ayb and annihilated them because they used to defraud people in measure and weight.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, said, threatening them: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day?﴾ Meaning: Do those not fear resurrection and standing before the One who knows secrets and inner thoughts, on a Day of great terror, abundant fright, and grave matter, in which whoever loses is cast into a scorching fire?

* *

His saying: ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: they will stand barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, in a station that is difficult, constricted, narrow, and distressing for the criminal, and there will overwhelm them, by the command of Allah, what powers and senses cannot bear.

Imam Malik said: From Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾, until one of them is submerged in his sweat up to the middle of his ears."

Al-Bukhari narrated it through the hadith of Malik and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Awn, both from Nafi', with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2862, 6531).]]. Muslim also narrated it through both routes. Likewise, Salih [and Thabit ibn Kaysan] [[Addition from A.]], Ayyub ibn Yahya, 'Abd Allah and 'Ubayd Allah the sons of 'Umar, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated it from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, with the same wording [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2862).]].

The wording of Imam Ahmad: Yazid narrated to us, Ibn Ishaq informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ out of the greatness of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, until the sweat reaches to the middle of their ears, bridling the men."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated to me, al-Miqdad—meaning Ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi—narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the sun will be brought near to the servants until it is a mile or two miles away. He said: The sun will scorch them, and they will be in sweat according to their deeds: some of them it will reach to their heels, some to their knees, some to their waists, and some it will bridle."

Muslim narrated it from al-Hakam ibn Musa, from Yahya ibn Hamzah, and al-Tirmidhi from Suwayd, from Ibn al-Mubarak—both from Ibn Jabir, with the same wording [[Musnad Ahmad (6/3), Sahih Muslim, no. (2864), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2421).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: al-Hasan ibn Sawwar narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, that Abu 'Abd al-Rahman told him, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sun will draw near on the Day of Resurrection to the distance of a mile, and its heat will be increased by such and such; the vermin will boil from it as cooking pots boil. They will sweat in it according to their sins: some of them will reach to their ankles, some to their shins, some to their middles, and some the sweat will bridle." Ahmad alone narrated it [[Musnad Ahmad (5/254).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Abu 'Ushshanah Hayy ibn Yu'min narrated to us, that he heard 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The sun will draw near to the earth, and people will sweat. Among the people, the sweat of some will reach their heels, some will reach half the shin, some will reach their knees, some will reach the buttocks, some will reach the waist, some will reach their shoulders, and some will reach the middle of the mouth"—and he gestured with his hand and placed it on his mouth; I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gesture like this—"and some will be covered by their sweat." And he struck with his hand as a gesture. Ahmad alone narrated it [[Musnad Ahmad (4/157).]].

It is also reported that they will stand for seventy years without speaking. It was said: they will stand three hundred years. It was said: they will stand forty thousand years. And judgment will be passed among them in the measure of ten [[In A: "a number of".]] thousand years, as in Sahih Muslim from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet: "On a day whose measure is fifty thousand years" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (987).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu 'Awn al-Ziyadi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam ibn 'Ajlan informed us, I heard Abu Yazid al-Madani, from Abu Hurayrah [[In M: "from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet".]], who said: The Prophet [[In M, A: "The Messenger of Allah".]] ﷺ said to Bashir [[In A: "Bashr".]] al-Ghifari: "How will you act on a day when people stand for three hundred years before the Lord of the worlds, by the days of the world, when no news from heaven reaches them and no command is given in it?" Bashir said: Allah is the One sought for help. He said: "When you lie down on your bed, seek refuge in Allah from the distress of the Day of Resurrection and the evil of the reckoning."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of 'Abd al-Salam, with the same wording [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/59).]].

In Sunan Abi Dawud: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge in Allah from the narrowness of the station on the Day of Resurrection [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (766), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]].

And from Ibn Mas'ud: they will stand forty years, with their heads raised toward the sky, no one speaking to them, the sweat having bridled both the righteous and the wicked among them.

And from Ibn 'Umar: they will stand a hundred years. Ibn Jarir narrated both [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/59).]].

In Sunan Abi Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from Azhar ibn Sa'id al-Hawwari, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from 'A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to open the night prayer by saying Allah is Greatest ten times, praising Him ten times, glorifying Him ten times, seeking forgiveness ten times, and saying: "O Allah, forgive me, guide me, provide for me, and grant me well-being," and he used to seek refuge from the narrowness of the station on the Day of Resurrection [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (766); Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/208); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1356).]].

For this reason He said: ﴿a spring from which those brought near will drink﴾, meaning: the brought-near ones drink it unmixed, while it is mixed for the companions of the right hand. This was said by Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Masruq, Qatadah, and others.

Allah the Exalted says: Indeed, ﴿the record of the righteous﴾ — and they are the opposite of the wicked — ﴿is in ʿIlliyyin﴾, meaning their destination is ʿIlliyyin, which is the opposite of Sijjin.

Al-Aʿmash narrated from Shamir ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked Kaʿb while I was present about Sijjin. He said: "It is the seventh earth, and in it are the spirits of the disbelievers." He also asked him about ʿIlliyyin, and he said: "It is the seventh heaven, and in it are the spirits of the believers." Likewise, more than one said: "It is the seventh heaven."

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾, that it means: Paradise.

Qatadah said: "ʿIlliyyun is the right side of the Throne's leg." Others said: "ʿIlliyyun is near the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha)."

For this reason He, magnifying its matter and exalting its status, said: ﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyun is?﴾ Then He said, confirming what was recorded for them: ﴿It is a written record, witnessed by those brought near (to Allah)﴾, and they are the angels, as Qatadah said.

Al-ʿAwfi said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "It is witnessed by the brought-near ones of every heaven."

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed the righteous will be in bliss﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection they will be in lasting bliss, and in gardens with abundant bounty, ﴿upon couches (al-arā'ik)﴾, which are thrones beneath canopies (al-ḥijāl), ﴿looking on﴾. It has been said: its meaning is that they look upon their dominion and what Allah has given them of good and bounty that never ends and never perishes. And it has been said: its meaning is ﴿upon couches, looking﴾ at Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is a contrast to what those wicked ones were described with: ﴿Nay, indeed they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾. So He mentions of these that they are granted the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while they are on their couches and carpets, as has preceded in the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "Indeed the lowest in station among the people of Paradise is one who looks over his dominion for a distance of two thousand years, seeing its farthest end just as he sees its nearest; and indeed the highest of them is one who looks upon Allah twice each day."
